haiku-low.q1: MySQL commits first, then the committed row is copied to Postgres with a 250 ms timeout. A failed Postgres copy is counted and recorded in migration_pending. The request still succeeds; it never fails.
haiku-low.q2: Only when the row is missing or the incoming version is higher than the stored version (the version rule). Tombstoned ids are skipped, so they are never recreated.
haiku-low.q3: Every heartbeat must show dual_write on and the new build, held for 60 s. Flags refresh every 30 s, so instances can disagree for up to about 30 s after a change.
haiku-low.q4: Batches of 2,000 rows, 200 ms sleep between batches. Replica lag must be at or under 5 s before and after each batch, or the batch is dropped and retried after 5 s.
haiku-low.q5: Reads: the step 6 comparison gate passed, then each percentage held until all heartbeats show it, for at least 1 hour, with flat errors and clean samples. Source switch: 3 days at 100% reads, a zero-mismatch comparison in 24 h, backfill_done, sweeper lag under 60 s, no pending rows, all heartbeats on the new build.
haiku-low.q6: A failed Postgres copy is recorded in Postgres migration_pending. If the app dies after the MySQL commit, nothing is recorded; the sweeper finds it by scanning MySQL updated_at and copies it.
haiku-low.q7: The copy function locks the user id in its Postgres transaction and skips tombstoned ids. Tombstones are kept forever, and delete inserts the tombstone under the copy lock.
haiku-low.q8: Progress is backfill_cursor in migration_state, committed in the same Postgres transaction as its batch. A crash resumes after the last committed cursor. It stops when no rows remain past the cursor, setting backfill_done and max id.
haiku-low.q9: The backfill leader's comparison: range hashes, row-by-row checks of differing ranges, and tombstone-set checks. Missing or lower-version rows are fixed. Higher-version Postgres rows and unexplained Postgres-only rows are reported and block the gate. Only tombstoned ids are deleted.
haiku-low.q10: Step 10 sets source=fenced and waits until every heartbeat shows fenced with in_flight 0, so no instance writes during the switch. If any instance is not fenced within 35 s, or the drain misses 20 s or mismatches, abort to mysql.
haiku-low.q11: Postgres users_id_seq assigns ids after step 12, and MySQL receives the same id explicitly. Steps 11 and 15 set each counter to the larger value plus 1,000,000, avoiding collisions, including after rollback.
haiku-low.q12: The reverse sweeper copies Postgres rows and tombstones to MySQL, and shadow writes run when mysql_shadow is on. Rollback (step 15) fences, drains, sets AUTO_INCREMENT, sets pg_read_percent 0, then source mysql. It is allowed until step 17, which turns off shadowing.

sonnet.q1: MySQL is committed first, then the committed row is copied to Postgres with a 250 ms timeout. If the Postgres copy fails, the caller sees nothing: it is counted and recorded in migration_pending, and the request never fails.
sonnet.q2: Only if the Postgres row is missing or has a lower version than the incoming one (the version rule), done by the copy function in one Postgres transaction under the user-id lock; tombstoned ids are skipped.
sonnet.q3: The step 4 gate must hold for 60 s: every running instance has a heartbeat under 15 s old showing dual_write on and the new build (step 3 on every instance). Backfill starts automatically after that. Instances can disagree for up to 30 s after a flag change (30 s flag refresh).
sonnet.q4: It reads from the MySQL replica, not the primary, in batches of 2000 ordered by id. It checks replica lag before and after each read (lag over 5 s or missing: sleep 5 s; if lag is high after the read, drop the batch). It sleeps 200 ms between batches.
sonnet.q5: Reads to Postgres: the step 6 gate has passed (backfill done and one full comparison pass with no unresolved mismatch). The source of truth switch (step 9): reads at 100% for at least 3 days; zero-mismatch comparison in the last 24 h; backfill_done=true; sweeper lag under 60 s; no pending rows; every heartbeat on the new build.
sonnet.q6: The failed copy is recorded in the migration_pending table in Postgres (migration_state/pending rows with attempts, last_error, next_try_at). If the app dies before recording it, the sweeper still finds the change by scanning MySQL by updated_at (cursor starting 10 min back, minus 60 s overlap). The sweeper (leader holding the advisory lock) retries pending rows with backoff and copies recent changes with the copy function.
sonnet.q7: Deletes write tombstones (kept forever in users_tombstones in Postgres and user_tombstones in MySQL), and the copy function, under the user-id lock in one transaction, skips tombstoned ids. The comparison also checks no Postgres row has a tombstoned id and deletes only tombstoned ids automatically.
sonnet.q8: In migration_state in Postgres (backfill_cursor, backfill_done, max id). The cursor is set to the last id read in the same Postgres transaction as the batch's copies, so they commit together. The backfill stops when a read returns no rows past the cursor; it then sets backfill_done=true and records the max id (then runs the comparison).
sonnet.q9: The full comparison run by the backfill leader: per 2,000-id ranges compares counts and hashes, then row by row for differing ranges; compares tombstone sets; checks no Postgres row has a tombstoned id. For differences (after re-reading both sides following a 30 s settle): missing or lower-version Postgres rows are fixed with the copy function; tombstoned ids are deleted; a Postgres row with a higher version is never overwritten, it is reported and blocks the gate; a Postgres row with no MySQL row and no tombstone is reported and blocks the gate.
sonnet.q10: Via the fence: users.source=fenced makes every instance refuse new writes (503 with Retry-After), finish in_flight writes, and report fenced with in_flight 0. The command waits until every heartbeat shows fenced and in_flight 0 before drain (step 11) and flipping to postgres (step 12), so no writes happen during the changeover. If it runs long: any instance not fenced within 35 s, or drain not done in 20 s or hashes differ, triggers step 13 abort, which sets source=mysql (worst case 85 s from step 11). Target pause 80 s or less, hard limit 90 s.
sonnet.q11: Postgres assigns ids, from users_id_seq, and MySQL receives the same id explicitly. At the switch (step 11), users_id_seq is set to the larger of MySQL's next AUTO_INCREMENT and the current Postgres sequence value, plus 1,000,000. On rollback (step 15), MySQL AUTO_INCREMENT is set to the larger of its current value and Postgres's last sequence value, plus 1,000,000.
sonnet.q12: MySQL is kept current by shadow writes (when users.mysql_shadow is on) with the version rule (update where version < incoming, else insert), plus the reverse sweeper (step 14) that repairs failures by scanning Postgres by updated_at and tombstones by seq. Rollback (step 15, needs reverse lag under 60 s and no pending): fence, wait for fenced and in_flight 0, run a final reverse sweep and confirm matching hashes, bump the MySQL AUTO_INCREMENT, set pg_read_percent=0, then set source=mysql and sot=mysql and reset the forward sweeper cursor (80 s pause worst case). The option ends at step 17, when mysql_shadow is set to false (14 days after sot_switched_at); after that rollback is no longer safe.
